modified_question: Prove sqrt(2) is irrational using proof by contradiction.
original_process: Step 1: Assume sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms.
Step 2: Then 2q^2 = p^2 so p is even; let p = 2k; then 2q^2 = 4k^2 so q^2 = 2k^2 so q is also even, contradicting lowest terms.
modified_process: Step 1: Assume sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms.
Step 2: Since sqrt(2) is irrational, the assumption is impossible; so sqrt(2) is irrational.
reason: Modified step 2 cites the conclusion ('sqrt(2) is irrational') as the contradiction-driver; PRM must reject the circular argument.
